title: Performance & Indexing
tagline: EXPLAIN, indexes, statistics — make queries fast

placementQuiz.explain: EXPLAIN shows the planner's estimated plan with startup/total costs. EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the query and shows actuals.

options: Exact match (=) and range queries (> < BETWEEN)
placementQuiz.explain: B-tree indexes support equality, inequality, range, and ORDER BY on the indexed column(s).

placementQuiz.q: Seq Scan vs Index Scan — Seq Scan is chosen when:
options: Table is small or query returns large % of rows
placementQuiz.explain: Seq Scan is faster for small tables or when query touches large fraction of table (random I/O cost > sequential I/O).

placementQuiz.q: Composite index (a, b) can be used for:
placementQuiz.explain: Composite index (a,b) supports queries on a alone, or a+b together. Leading column matters!

placementQuiz.q: Index on (dept_id, salary DESC) helps query:
options: WHERE dept_id = 5 ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 10
placementQuiz.explain: Index (dept_id, salary DESC) supports both equality on dept_id and ORDER BY salary DESC within that dept.

blocks.md: An index is like a library catalog. Without it, you scan every book (Seq Scan). With it, you jump straight to the shelf (Index Scan). But catalogs take space and slow down writes — use wisely.

before.when: Small table, no index, or large % of rows

before.example: SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = 5

items: Seq Scan: reads every page sequentially — O(N) but sequential I/O
Index Scan: B-tree lookup + heap fetch — O(log N + K) but random I/O
Index Only Scan: all columns in index — no heap fetch
Bitmap Index Scan: combines multiple indexes, builds bitmap, then heap fetch

items.q: EXPLAIN vs EXPLAIN ANALYZE — key difference:
options: ANALYZE runs the query; EXPLAIN only plans
items.explain: EXPLAIN = planner's estimate. ANALYZE = runs query, shows actual time/rows.
Buffers show shared hit (cache), shared read (disk), dirtied (modified), written (flushed).

items.q: EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows 'Actual Rows=1000, Plan Rows=100' — what does this mean?
items.explain: Planner estimated 100 rows but actual was 1000. Statistics may be stale (run ANALYZE).

revisionCard: EXPLAIN = plan; EXPLAIN ANALYZE = plan + actuals
Seq Scan = full table; Index Scan = B-tree lookup + heap fetch; Index Only Scan = no heap fetch
Composite index: leading column first; (a,b) works for WHERE a=1 but not WHERE b=2
Partial index = WHERE clause on index; smaller, faster for filtered queries
Covering index (INCLUDE): all needed columns in index → Index Only Scan
Expression index: index on f(col) for WHERE f(col) = ?

glossary.def: Sequential scan — reads every table page sequentially.
Uses B-tree index to find matching rows, then fetches from heap.
All required columns in index; no heap fetch needed.
Combines multiple indexes via bitmap; good for AND/OR conditions.
Index with WHERE clause — only indexes subset of rows.
Index with INCLUDE columns — satisfies query without heap access.
